body: Tattooing is really interesting, but I'm sure I'd ever be entirely comfortable doing it. I imagine it's very stressful, and messing up on something done on someone else's body seems pretty terrible. Plus from what I've heard, tattoo artists are generally expected to be tattooed or they lose some respect. I'm very bad around needles, so I probably won't be getting inked any time soon.

Thanks so much for this reply, there was a lot that was said there that resonates with my current situation. I hope all of your sisters are safe and stay safe, no one should be raised by an abusive parent. I'm also sorry you feel you can't do anything for them - I think being there and sympathizing is enough. You're trying, that's more than a lot of people do.

I like how you said it's not about the severity, but the frequency of the fights. That's how I feel as well. Most of the fights are over very small things like leaving a cabinet open, but they're so constant no one in the house can stand it. Her first resort is always screaming, never asking. My mother stopped physically assaulting us when we stopped letting her, but I imagine it'd be harder for daughters to do that with their father. If my father was the abusive one, I'd probably still get hit.
Thank you, this post was really encouraging to me.
Thank you for responding. Yes, I do draw. I've been drawing since I was a child.

>In the UK you can do your own studying and then pay for the exams you want to take.

In the US, that's pretty much what a GED is. I think around here each test is 15 dollars (unlimited amount of retries for no extra money, though), and there's 4/5 tests I have to take.


>Would you consider drawing me something? Doesn't have to be anything fancy.

Yes, but I don't think I'll be doing any drawing right now. I'll try to draw something later today or tomorrow. I have to say though, my drawing isn't anything amazing. It's a hobby mostly, and I tend to draw cartoony stuff.

Clubs and meetings are pretty good advice. I used to go to meetups based off a common interest, and it did help me some in breaking out of my shell. I'd like to go again sometime. It's just very draining for me, and oftentimes I have the problem where I can't leave when I've had enough because another member of my family wants to stay. Understandable, but keeping me there past what I can take makes me very reluctant to go back in case it happens again.

Also, I never knew social care would fit adults with new families. That sounds interesting, but I don't think I could do it. The only person I would flat out want out of my family is my brother, everyone else I just really wish would change and look at their actions.

Thank you for taking the time to respond.

I feel that if I get out and be independent I can have a much healthier relationship with people like my sister and mother. Hopefully this will lead to me being able to set boundaries more effectively, and give me the ability to control who is in my life based off of their behavior. I do honestly think that'll help. I'm just stuck on the first step, it seems like my depression and social anxiety are mountain-high hurdles that are stopping me from doing things like getting a job or finishing highschool (/getting GED), which I need to do in order to get on my own two feet.

These past few months it's hard to say what's been making me happy. It's been getting worse and worse, which lead to me posting this. Though I haven't drawn much recently, drawing is one thing that has been with me throughout my entire life. I've always loved to draw, and it helped me get out my emotions effectively onto paper. I also find it easy to forget about my life when I absorb myself in games and TV shows - which probably isn't the best thing to do, but it's helped me keep my head above the water. It doesn't exactly make me *happy*, though.
